prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which bifunctional PROTAC molecules and molecular glues recruit ubiquitin ligases to eliminate chosen proteins

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single-topic prize for targeted protein degradation to Crews, Deshaies and Handa. Induced proximity is a molecular-design principle: a small molecule is turned into an adaptor that makes the cell's own ubiquitin ligase remove a protein of our choosing. That moves pharmacology from occupancy to event-driven removal and reaches proteins with no occupiable active site. The principle is shown by ternary-complex structures, degradation kinetics and independent reproduction in many laboratories, and thalidomide-class glues are already in medical use, so the mechanism is established even though the PROTAC clinical verdict is pending. Having read round 1, I would write the citation to name both PROTACs and molecular glues explicitly. This answers the chair's question on framing and the concern that two prizes are squeezed into one: Crews and Deshaies conceived the rationally designed bifunctional strand, and Handa identified cereblon, which explains why the glue strand works. Both strands act through the same mechanism, and the prize records that.
statement.case_against: No degrader drug is approved, so a committee that wants clinical confirmation could fairly call this one or a few years early. The three-name limit leaves out Ciulli (VHL ligands and structures that made degraders usable molecules), Sakamoto and Kim (the first PROTAC), Gray and Ito, each with a defensible claim. Handa anchors the glue strand rather than the PROTAC concept, so the trio is a compromise. If the committee judges that only a mature, cleanly attributed discovery should be recognised now, B038 or B057 would be the more conservative choice, and I could accept either.

responses.point: Xiaodong says her reservations about B066 concern attribution and timing, not science, that the C-N coupling prize has none of those problems, and that she would want the molecular-glue and PROTAC parts framed separately before committing.
responses.response: I accept the fairness of the attribution and timing objections, and they are the reason B038 stays as my first alternative. I disagree with framing the strands separately. Separate parts would need at least four names, which exceeds the three-person limit. They would also hide what the two strands share: both recruit an E3 ligase to a protein it would not normally ubiquitinate, and the structural work on cereblon and VHL shows this directly. I would keep one citation naming both and treat the omission of Ciulli, Sakamoto, Kim and Gray as the cost of the three-name limit, not as a flaw in the science. I also still ask what C-N coupling lets chemists do that they could not do after 2010. Her answer on Kosugi's priority is reasonable, but it does not change my view that B066 opens more.

responses.point: Peter finds the PROTAC concept more compelling than the glue mechanism, says the two strands have different originators, and could support B066 if the committee settles the framing.
responses.response: This is the most useful challenge to my position. On originators I agree: Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated the designed bifunctional molecule, while thalidomide acting through cereblon was discovered, with Handa explaining the mechanism. I would meet his request for a settled framing by anchoring the citation on the shared principle of recruiting ubiquitin ligases to eliminate chosen proteins, with the glue strand explained by Handa's cereblon work. If the committee finds the glue strand too different, the fallback is Crews and Deshaies with Ciulli, which gives a purer PROTAC prize. I did not move to it because the glue mechanism is the part already validated in patients. I would still rather present the principle than force a choice between the two strands.

responses.point: Johan will not let B066 override a mature, cleanly attributable discovery like sequencing, given the three-laureate limit, and notes that eight names are credited on the ballot.
responses.response: Mature and cleanly attributable is a fair test, and sequencing passes the first half. It does not clearly pass the second, since Balasubramanian and Klenerman would be paired against Rothberg, Mayer and Ju, which Andrei also flagged, and some members see the field as technology or medicine rather than chemical design. The ballot's eight names are an ordering of the field, not our proposal: our proposal is three people and a citation. Where I agree with Johan is that overdue recognition counts for something, which is why B057 stays among my alternatives. On balance I still weigh a discovery that created a new class of chemical tools and drugs above one whose main weakness is a split in platform credit.

responses.point: Heiner has not resolved whether Ciulli should replace Handa, and raised a two-part prize such as B066 with B022 or B057.
responses.response: On Ciulli versus Handa, I considered the swap. Ciulli's VHL ligands and structures made PROTACs drug-like, and that claim is strong. But replacing Handa removes the cereblon work that explains the best-validated degraders in medicine, and the citation would then cover only the PROTAC half. I keep Handa and accept that this is a contestable choice. On a two-part prize: with Crews, Deshaies and Handa filling the three-name limit, a second part would need to add no new people, which B022 and B057 do not allow. I therefore treat B066 as a single-topic proposal.

responses.point: Andrei calls B066 possibly one or a few years early, with the committee able to prefer fully mature sequencing, and asks whether PROTACs and glues are one or two achievements.
responses.response: I take his timing worry seriously. It is the point on which I am least certain, and I hold the position on the strength of the mechanism: independent structures, kinetics and glues in clinical use. Clinical readouts on degraders could still change the weight I give it, but the committee has recognised confirmed principles before the last clinical milestone. On one or two achievements, I would count them as one because the same chemistry applies: a molecule that brings a ligase to its substrate. I would also add, as Andrei does, that the committee should say openly that the PROTAC and glue strands have different originators.

uncertainties: Whether the absence of an approved degrader drug is enough reason to postpone recognition by a year or more.
Whether the trio Crews, Deshaies and Handa is better than Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli, and whether the citation should name PROTACs and glues together.
Whether a committee majority would prefer the mature, cleanly attributed B038 over B066 in the final vote, which I could accept.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict requiring recusal. My postdoc mentors (Stevens, Boey) and my Linköping group are not among the credited names for B066 or my alternatives (B038, B057). My topical overlap with Emma Sparr on peptide and lipid self-assembly is not a tie to any candidate, and I have no personal or institutional link to any shortlisted person.
